chief_complaint: Cystic fibrosis with associated diabetes, chronic kidney disease and related metabolic complications
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 36‑year‑old man with cystic fibrosis diagnosed in childhood, complicated by chronic Pseudomonas airway colonisation, a sepsis episode in 2007, and recurrent sinusitis. He has longstanding diabetes mellitus (type 2 and CF‑related) with micro‑albuminuria, disorder of kidney due to diabetes and stage 2 chronic kidney disease. Hypertension (stage 1) and hypertriglyceridemia are present, as is anemia of unclear etiology. He reports hand osteoarthritis treated with naproxen. Socially, he experiences intimate‑partner abuse, lives in unsatisfactory housing, has only primary‑school education, a criminal record and a military service background, all of which may affect adherence and follow‑up. The most recent visit (2008) documented ongoing management of these conditions but shows gaps in cardiovascular and renal protective therapy.

active_problems.name: Diabetes mellitus due to cystic fibrosis

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior part‑time employment, episodes of stress, limited social contact, gingivitis (resolved 2007), and multiple earlier medication‑review entries. These reflect historical psychosocial stressors but no additional chronic medical diagnoses beyond those listed as active.
